question: How does moving a fixed rehearsal dose from before reporting to after reporting affect retention and recovery under the frozen memory harness?
observed: Across the frozen dose sweep, shifting rehearsal toward the post-report side increased post-report recovery.
At the all-post-report endpoint, final mean old retention reached about 0.8944 versus about 0.8778 at the all-pre-report endpoint in the shown assignment.
The qualification harness classified the run as a qualified scientific result.
established: Rehearsal timing relative to reporting changes retention/recovery behavior under this frozen harness.
A fully post-report allocation can outperform the fully pre-report allocation on the measured old-retention endpoint.
not_established: The result does not establish a universal optimal rehearsal schedule.
The result does not establish an autonomous self-improvement loop.
frozen_constraints: Do not retune thresholds, seeds, splits, or memory capacity after observing the result.
Preserve the experiment's fixed rehearsal-dose budget when comparing timing effects.
next_seams: Separate the effect of rehearsal timing from rehearsal-history structure and capacity competition.
